diagnostic_evidence.quote: The kernel $\kappa$ is differentiable, and there exists a symmetric kernel $\bar{\kappa}: \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 1 requires κ to be differentiable everywhere with ∇₂κ(x,y)=(x−y)κ̄(x,y). For κ(x,y)=φ(‖x−y‖) this needs φ differentiable at 0 with φ'(0)=0 (so that κ is differentiable on the diagonal and κ̄(x,x)=−lim φ'(r)/r exists). A φ that is merely continuously differentiable almost everywhere does not guarantee this: e.g. the Matérn kernel with ν=1/2 (φ(r)=e^{−r/σ}) is not differentiable at x=y, so 'Matérn kernels' in general do not satisfy the assumption, only those with ν>1/2 (and IMQ/Gaussian).

failure_location.quote: \Cref{assumption:gradient_kappa} is satisfied by many distance-based kernels defined as $\kappa(x,y) = \varphi(\|x-y\|)$ for some function $\varphi:\mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$ that is continuously differentiable almost everywhere. This includes the Gaussian kernel, the inverse multiquadric kernel (IMQ) and Matérn kernels.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by: φ differentiable on [0,∞) with φ'(0)=0 and φ'(r)/r extending continuously to r=0; restrict 'Matérn kernels' to ν>1/2.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised class of kernels covered by the theory (Props 3.2, Thm 3.3, Cor 3.4 and the MSIP map) is overstated; results do not apply to non-smooth radial kernels such as Matérn ν=1/2. The kernels actually used (Gaussian, Matérn ν=1.5) are unaffected.
issues.title: Scope claim for Assumption 1 (a.e.-differentiable radial profiles, all Matérn kernels) is not supported
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of the scope condition fixes it; all results and experiments survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Under the assumption that the kernel matrices $\bm{K}(\yt)$ and $\bm{\bar{K}}(\yt)$ are non-singular, the relationship \eqref{eq:msip_fixed_point_def} is expressed as a fixed-point iteration

issues.failure_explanation: Ψ_MSIP inverts the diagonal matrix W(Y)=diag(ŵ(Y)), ŵ(Y)=K(Y)^{-1}v₀(Y). Nonsingularity of K(Y) and K̄(Y) does not imply ŵ_i(Y)≠0 for all i (optimal kernel quadrature weights can vanish or change sign), so the stated hypotheses do not make the fixed-point iteration well defined; the linear system (eq:msip_fixed_point_def) is then singular and Y^{(t+1)} is not determined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that all ŵ_i(Y^{(t)})≠0 (equivalently W(Y^{(t)}) nonsingular), as is already done implicitly in Theorem 3.3's second equality, and note how the iteration handles a particle with zero weight.
issues.overall_effect: The fixed-point iteration and its rewriting as preconditioned gradient descent (eq:fixed_point_as_precond_grad_descent) are only defined on configurations where every ŵ_i(Y^{(t)})≠0; the paper's stated well-definedness condition is incomplete.
issues.title: MSIP map Ψ_MSIP requires nonzero optimal weights, not only nonsingular K and K̄
issues.why_classification: Adding the missing local non-degeneracy condition restores every stated guarantee without new arguments.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $m \in [M]$, we recall that $\nabla\kappa$ is bounded on $\X\times\X$ to find

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem assumes only Assumption 1, but the proof (i) writes F_M via ŵ(Y)=K(Y)^{-1}v₀(Y) and differentiates K(Y)^{-1}, which requires K(Y) invertible on X^M_≠ (true for strictly positive definite kernels but not assumed), and (ii) differentiates v₀ under the integral by 'recalling' that ∇κ is bounded, a hypothesis stated only in Proposition 3.2 and absent from the theorem.

failure_location.quote: Under \Cref{assumption:gradient_kappa}, the gradient of $F$, seen as an $M \times d$ matrix, is given by

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to the theorem: κ strictly positive definite (so K(Y) is invertible on X^M_≠ and F_M is differentiable there) and ∇κ bounded (or another domination condition permitting differentiation under the integral).
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the gradient formula and the preconditioned-gradient-descent interpretation are not established for kernels with singular Gram matrices or unbounded gradients; the corollary inherits the same gap.
issues.title: Theorem 3.3 omits hypotheses its proof relies on (invertibility of K(Y), bounded ∇κ for differentiating v₀)
issues.why_classification: Standard hypotheses, already used elsewhere in the paper, close the gap with no change to the conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: Since F_M(Y)=½(C_π − ⟨ŵ,Kŵ⟩), one has 2∇_{ij}F_M = −2⟨ŵ,K∇ŵ⟩ − ⟨ŵ,∇Kŵ⟩, but (eq:gradient_optimal_mmd_identity) drops the minus sign (and the initial expansion of F_M has +2⟨ŵ,v₀⟩ instead of −2⟨ŵ,v₀⟩). Consequently (eq:grad_F_pi_first) is the negative of the true gradient. Combining (eq:grad_F_pi_first), (eq:w_hat_grad_K_w_hat_final) and (eq:w_hat_grad_v_final) as the proof says would give +2ŵ_i(...), yet (eq:2times_gradient_FM) writes −2ŵ_i(...) with no justification. Two compensating sign errors make the chain of equalities invalid as written, although the final formula is correct (it is confirmed for M=1 with a Gaussian kernel by direct computation of ∇F₁).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing minus signs in the F_M expansion and in (eq:gradient_optimal_mmd_identity)/(eq:grad_F_pi_first) so that 2∇_{ij}F_M = −2⟨ŵ,∇_{ij}v₀⟩ + ⟨ŵ,∇_{ij}Kŵ⟩, which then consistently yields (eq:2times_gradient_FM).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the main gradient identity contains an invalid step; the theorem's conclusion itself is correct, so downstream uses are not affected once the proof is corrected.
issues.title: Sign inconsistency in the proof of Theorem 3.3 (compensating errors)
issues.why_classification: Purely local sign corrections restore a valid derivation of an already-correct statement.

issues.failure_explanation: For M=1, Ψ_MSIP(y) = (κ(y,y)/(v₀(y)κ̄(y,y)))(v̄₁(y)+ū(y)) = y + (κ(y,y)/(v₀(y)κ̄(y,y)))(v̄₁(y) − v̄₀(y)y), whereas Ψ_MS(y) = v̄₁/v̄₀ = y + (1/v̄₀(y))(v̄₁(y) − v̄₀(y)y). These maps coincide only when κ(y,y)v̄₀(y)=v₀(y)κ̄(y,y), which holds for the Gaussian kernel (κ̄=λκ) but not for general kernels satisfying Assumption 1 (e.g. IMQ, Matérn). The paper's argument only shows the two maps share fixed points (critical points of F₁), which does not make mean shift a special case of the MSIP iteration; the claim (echoed in the abstract's 'MSIP extends the (non-interacting) mean shift algorithm') is established only for the Gaussian kernel.

failure_location.quote: Then, the mean shift algorithm becomes a special case of the fixed-point iteration defined in \Cref{sec:msip} when $M = 1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the special-case statement to the Gaussian (squared-exponential) kernel, and for general kernels state only that mean shift and M=1 MSIP have the same fixed points (critical points of F₁).
issues.overall_effect: The general 'mean shift is MSIP with M=1' identification is overstated; for non-Gaussian kernels MSIP with M=1 is a differently scaled iteration with the same fixed points.
issues.title: Mean shift is claimed to be a special case of MSIP for M=1, but for non-Gaussian kernels only the fixed points coincide
issues.why_classification: A precise restatement of scope suffices; the Gaussian case and the fixed-point correspondence, which carry the conceptual content, remain valid.
